Explaining the upside and downside of D-Waves new quantum computer. (Ars)

Tl; dr---- The D-wave computer is now 1,000 times faster than a regular computer. It basically works on magnets flipping poles many times until it reaches its lowest energy state. Once it does, the cumulative direction of each magnetic pole is the solution to the problem. There are now 2,000 qubits instead of 1,000 but roughly 800 of those qubits are dedicated to the interconnectivity of all the qubits. The other 1,200 of them are dedicated to solving the problem / program.

The cost of running the quantum computer is cheaper than running a supercomputer of the same power and most of the cost comes from running the silicon wafer at milli Kelvin temperatures.

The article didn't really cover what types of problems the quantum computer can solve, but the author remarked that he was afraid about these machines being able to decrypt HTTPS encryption to his bank and accessing his bank account. And if it's not D-wave that would do this, it would certainly be somebody else. I'm personally curious what these computers are capable of, however, as far as what problems they can solve besides decryption.

Edit: I looked on their website, and it seems that the types of problems it can solve is nothing really impressive. It includes things like: radiotherapy optimization, protein folding, water network optimization, machine learning, object detection, labeling news stories, video compression, and Monte Carlo simulations which is an accounting problem solver. It looks like AI is not within our grasp just yet.
